subheading: Rare earths, lithium & the Western supply-chain onshoring trade
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Mining/minerals names carry commodity-price, dilution, and geopolitical risk. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.sub: THAW HOPES DRAIN THE SCARCITY PREMIUM FROM WESTERN RARE-EARTH NAMES (SEP 2 – OCT 1)
kpis.label: MP Materials fell from $54.70 to $46.08 over the 30 days to Oct 1, VanEck's REMX dropped 17% and USA Rare Earth 23%, while the S&P 500 was roughly flat. The selloff is sector-wide, not company-specific: any sign of a US-China thaw trims the premium investors pay for Western supply. MP closed near $46.96 on Oct 2 with 18.85% of float sold short, $146M of insider selling over 12 months and a Q2 revenue print of $108.5M (+89% YoY). MP also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

kpis.sub: CHINA'S SUSPENDED EXPORT CONTROLS LAPSE IN ~37 DAYS UNLESS EXTENDED
kpis.label: Beijing's Oct 2025 controls — which reach foreign-made products containing as little as 0.1% Chinese rare-earth content by value — remain suspended only until Nov 10, 2026. Analysts note a diplomatic truce cannot substitute for Western separation plants, metallization capacity and qualified magnets, which remain largely absent. Pr-Nd oxide held firm but quiet on Sep 29 ahead of China's National Day holiday

kpis.sub: LITHIUM CARBONATE FUTURES SLIP BACK DOWN (GFEX, OCT 4)
kpis.label: Guangzhou lithium carbonate futures sat near $18,314/t on Oct 4, down from roughly $20,010/t spot on Sep 22 and well below May's ~$27,000/t peak; SP Angel quoted $19,161/t on Oct 2. The Sep restocking bounce has faded — Albemarle is down 26% year-to-date at $104.62 and Lithium Americas is at its 52-week low

kpis.sub: FREEPORT STILL AT ITS ANALYST TARGET AS GRASBERG RECOVERS SLOWLY (OCT 2)
kpis.label: Freeport guided Q3 copper output near 830M lb and sales above $6.50/lb realized, but deferred 60,000 oz of gold sales to Q4, lifting unit costs ~5% above the July $2.00/lb estimate. Grasberg mill throughput averaged ~140,000 t/day, about 67% of pre-incident rates, with 80% targeted by mid-2027. LME copper eased to ~$14,244/t on Oct 2 after a Codelco fatality paused crushing; the stock sits at the $72.87 average target

themes.title: Markets price a US-China thaw that the Nov 10 cliff says is unfinished
themes.description: After the Xi summit gave 'relief, not resolution,' rare-earth equities kept sliding through September: MP -15.8%, REMX -17% and USAR -23% over 30 days. Yet the underlying structure hasn't moved — China's controls are only suspended until Nov 10, 2026, and cover foreign products with 0.1% Chinese rare-earth content. Whether the pause is extended is now the sector's single biggest binary, and it cuts both ways: an extension may further deflate the scarcity premium, while a lapse would re-inflate it.

themes.title: Glencore and Mercuria commit $1B to the US critical-minerals stockpile
themes.description: On Sep 23, Glencore and Mercuria became the first participants in VaultCo, the independently governed company behind Project Vault, committing $1B to procure and stockpile critical minerals. The vehicle rests on $10B of EXIM financing plus roughly $2B of private capital, and CSIS calls the move a transition from designing the financial architecture to building the physical supply chain. Demand-side support is real, but who sells into the Vault matters: trader-led procurement does not automatically favor US producers.

themes.title: Floors now reach heavy rare earths — but only for projects that exist
themes.description: The Pentagon's $110/kg magnet-related NdPr floor anchors MP Materials, and an Aug 2026 $1.55B Brazil deal locked the first price floors on dysprosium and terbium. Such floors insulate funded producers from Chinese undercutting, yet a floor is only worth something to a company that has product to sell, and the Pentagon's 2027 defense-supply deadline keeps pushing timelines. Policy dependency is both the moat and the risk for the whole group.

rows.angle: Only US rare-earth mine + processing (Mountain Pass); $500M Apple magnet offtake (shipments from 2027) + DoD price floor and equity backing (DoD the largest shareholder)
rows.watch for: Traded ~$46.96 on Oct 2, down ~16% in 30 days with the sector. Q2 revenue was $108.5M (+89% YoY, beating $96.9M estimates) but EPS was -$0.01 and operating margin about -17%; short interest is 18.85% of float and insiders sold $146M over 12 months. Consensus is Moderate Buy with a ~$75 target, though Deutsche Bank, Needham and Baird all cut targets over the summer. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

rows.angle: Largest non-China rare-earth producer (Australia/Malaysia); pushing into heavy rare earths
rows.watch for: Amanda Lacaze left in late August after ~12 years and no permanent CEO has been named. FY26 REO output hit a record 13,089t, but NdPr was only 7,260t against 10,500t nameplate, so earnings stay sensitive to depressed NdPr prices. The ~A$294M heavy-rare-earth facility is progressing (samarium oxide started March 2026), and the Malaysian licence runs to 2036 with a condition to end radioactive waste generation by ~2031

Shares closed $104.62 on Oct 2 — down 26% year-to-date and near the lower half of an $85.85–$221 52-week range — as lithium carbonate futures slid back to ~$18.3k/t. Consensus is Moderate Buy with a ~$188 target, a gap that reflects cycle uncertainty more than conviction. Q3 results arrive Nov 4; incoming CEO Ragnar Udd starts Feb 1, 2027

rows.angle: Copper — the electrification metal at scale
rows.watch for: Closed ~$72.07 on Oct 2 (+4% that day, +42% YTD), essentially at the $72.87 average target, with a $103.5B market cap and a ~35x P/E. Q3 copper output held near 830M lb, but 60,000 oz of gold sales slipped to Q4 and Grasberg runs at ~67% of pre-incident rates, with full capacity not due until end-2027. A Codelco fatality is tightening supply while Chinese demand softens, and the Section 232 refined-copper tariff decision remains open

rows.angle: US rare-earth mine-to-magnet aspirant; Texas mine + Oklahoma magnet plant + Serra Verde combination; DoC $1.6B LOI + ~10% equity stake (Jan 2026)
rows.watch for: Thras Moraitis became CEO on Oct 1 as the company reorganizes into three business units. The Blacksburg, SC $1.2B magnet facility is under construction; a DOE separation pilot grant adds support

rows.angle: Uranium + rare-earth processing at White Mesa; Australian Strategic Materials deal adds metals, Dubbo and US alloy plans
rows.watch for: Closed $10.73 on Oct 2, right at its $10.64 52-week low and down 26% YTD, on a $2.8B market cap. Consensus is Moderate Buy (5 buy, 1 hold, 1 sell) with a ~$21.85 target. The company is still unprofitable, so the vertical-integration story still has to turn into cash flow while rare-earth prices stay depressed

Shares closed $2.54 on Oct 2 — at the 52-week low ($2.51) and down 41.6% YTD, with a ~$920M market cap. Consensus is Hold (3 buy, 7 hold, 1 sell) and short interest rose again. Thacker Pass construction continues toward a late-2027 mechanical-completion date, but the case rides on a lithium price that is sliding again

rows.angle: Early-stage Tanbreez (Greenland) rare earths and lithium projects
rows.watch for: ~$1.1B market cap on roughly $2M of exploration-related revenue; has been lifted by Greenland security agreements and refinery-expansion plans. Pure development risk with no producing asset

bear_case.title: The premium is deflating faster than the supply chain is being built
bear_case.description: Rare-earth equities fell 16–23% in 30 days on thaw hopes alone, which shows how much of the group's value is a geopolitical scarcity premium rather than cash flow. MP is still loss-making at the operating line (about -17% margin) on a P/S near 20x, and Western separation, metallization and magnet capacity remain thin ahead of the Nov 10 expiry. If Beijing extends the suspension, the premium may keep compressing before real capacity arrives.

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate futures are back near $18.3k/t versus a May peak of ~$27,000/t, and Albemarle and Lithium Americas are down 26% and 42% year-to-date. Freeport trades at its analyst target after a 42% gain, with Grasberg only ~67% restored and copper softening on weaker Chinese demand. A producer can be an excellent business at the wrong point in its price cycle.

bear_case.title: China can flood, freeze or consolidate
bear_case.description: Beijing's controls are suspended, not repealed, and can return on Nov 10 or be traded away in a deal. A flood of cheap Chinese NdPr would undercut non-Chinese producers even with Pentagon floors, since the floors only protect projects that already have product. Lynas' NdPr output at 7,260t versus 10,500t nameplate shows how price-sensitive even the established non-China producers are.

bear_case.title: Junior dilution, leadership gaps and policy dependency
bear_case.description: USAR, UUUU and LAC all trade at or near 52-week lows while funding multi-year builds, and equity raises are the standard way juniors fill the gap. Lynas has no permanent CEO and Albemarle's arrives in Feb 2027. The Vault, EXIM funding and DoD floors are real but discretionary: each can be re-scoped by a future administration, and Vault's first buyers are commodity traders, not US producers.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Still the only US mine-to-magnet producer with Apple and DoD anchors and Q2 revenue up 89% to $108.5M, but at ~$47 after a 16% 30-day slide, 18.85% short interest and a ~20x P/S it is held as Core on business quality, not price — and with Nov 10 as the key binary. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: White Mesa plus the ASM deal build a real integrated rare-earth platform, yet the stock sits at its $10.64 52-week low, down 26% YTD, still unprofitable, so it stays a small speculative position.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Blacksburg construction and a DOE pilot grant are real, but the shares have fallen 23% in 30 days to $13.59 on dilution risk and a CEO handover on Oct 1 — optionality with a genuine chance of zero.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: Thacker Pass is still the largest US lithium build, but the stock sits at its $2.51 52-week low with lithium futures back near $18.3k/t and 7 of 11 analysts at Hold, so size is kept to the smallest in the sleeve.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Excellent copper business but at $72.07 it trades essentially at the $72.87 average target after a 42% YTD run, with Grasberg only ~67% restored and gold-sale deferrals lifting unit costs ~5% — a top-of-cycle price, not an entry point.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: Lithium futures have slid back to ~$18.3k/t and ALB is down 26% YTD at $104.62; the cycle has not clearly bottomed and Q3 results on Nov 4 plus a CEO who arrives Feb 2027 leave too many open questions.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: Record FY26 output of 13,089t REO, but NdPr ran at 7,260t against 10,500t nameplate in a depressed price market and Lacaze's departure left no permanent CEO — good business, unresolved question.

positions.name: Critical Metals
positions.note: A ~$1.1B market cap on about $2M of exploration revenue and no producing asset; the research does not support owning pre-revenue Greenland optionality in a sector that just lost 16–23% on sentiment alone.
